subject: dragonfly
reasoning:
I'm thinking through the dragonfly's proportions at a real-world scale, around 6-7 cm body length, and deciding on a perched pose standing on its legs with wings spread out to the sides in resting position.

Now I'm sketching the skeleton hierarchy: a thorax root joint, a neck and head joint with a hinged jaw for mandibles, and a long curved abdomen chain built from a sequence of small segments running backward from the thorax.

For the abdomen I'm sweeping a tube along that chain with a tapering radius profile—wider near the base and narrowing toward the tip—then applying a striped blue/black paint pattern along its length to mimic dragonfly banding.

Adding stripe wobble and custom paint...

For the thorax, I'm using a scaled sphere with flat shading, elongated and positioned just above the abdomen's base.

For the body coloring, I'm applying diagonal stripe patterns in yellow-green and dark tones along the thorax sides. For the head, I'm placing two large spheres as compound eyes with a blue-green gradient, plus smaller shapes for the frons, labrum, and jaw details.

I'm thinking through faceted spheres for the eyes and ensuring part placement respects bone attachment and coordinate transforms. For legs, I'm planning six limbs attached underneath the thorax, each built as a three-segment chain extending forward from the body.

Working out leg joint coordinates per limb...

I'm setting up the leg tube geometry with Catmull-Rom knots and a tapering radius array for a thin, five-sided profile, mirroring the shape for the opposite leg. I'm adjusting the foot endpoint and radius slightly so the rounded cap sits just at ground level without dipping below it, and deciding to skip tiny spines or claws on the legs for now before moving on to the wings.

Now for the four wings, I'm extruding an outline along the X-axis with the extrusion plane defined by X and Z directions, working out the cross product to get correct normals so each wing's thickness points outward properly for both left and right sides.

Still defining wing outline points...

For coloring, I'm thinking a pale translucent-looking wing tone with a vein pattern layered using a patches approach—dark thin lines for veins over a light background fill.

I'm defining a custom paint function using surface coordinates to add realistic details: a dark pterostigma spot near the leading edge tip, positioned using the span and chord coordinates to mark that characteristic dark mark found on real wings.

Now I'm setting up the four wing joints on the thorax, positioning fore and hind wings at different z-offsets with swept-forward and swept-back orientations for left and right sides, letting the code orthogonalize the axes automatically.

I'm checking that the thorax top sits around y 0.028 so wings attach slightly embedded at y 0.026, and verifying legs and body proportions don't clip the floor. I'm also making sure the wing mesh's weighting references the joint's position correctly via the `at` parameter.

Now I'm adding cerci spikes at the abdomen tip bound to the last abdomen joint, confirming the abdomen's front segment overlaps the thorax's rear end so the sweep connects cleanly, and starting on the head's neck joint and face block parts.

For the head itself, I'm placing the big front-facing eye spheres, a small green frons bump between them, and building the jaw with upper labrum and lower lip boxes positioned around a jaw joint so the mandibles sit just below.

Now I'm adding tiny antenna rods anchored near the top of the head, and considering simple countershading paint for the eyes with a dark-to-green gradient, keeping everything flat-shaded and low-poly without extra highlight details.

For the thorax, I'm scaling a low-poly sphere into an elongated body shape positioned above the legs, then designing a custom paint function that darkens the top surface and adds oblique green stripe patterns along the sides based on position.

Writing abdomen segment banding...

Then I set up the chain path for the tail using a curved spline, creating 6 abdomen bones plus cerci attached to the thorax.

For the neck, head, and jaw I add explicit role labels so the rig recognizes them properly, and I give the wing joint a hinge role with its axis along the bone's local X direction. For the legs, I'm defining four-point catmull paths that create three spans each, naming the joints hip, knee, ankle, and foot per leg (prefixed by side like FL), all parented to the thorax.

I'm sweeping each limb chain into tubes with tapering radii, thicker at the femur and narrowing toward the foot, mirrored left-to-right by flipping the X sign per side, and then finalizing the rig export by returning the root bone. For coloring, I'm defining paint functions that return color values from position and normal, using a patch-based texture for the wing interior with a subtle amber tint near the base.

Now I'm setting up wing extrusion options including thickness, smoothing, and the joint it's bound to, placing wing hinge joints relative to the thorax with directional offsets based on side, and establishing the thorax root joint position as the parent for all limb chains before finalizing the code.
